scenario: A high-altitude expedition company recruits porters who exhibit proven altitude acclimatisation capacity OR exceptional load-carrying capacity. The two traits are independent in the applicant pool; the OR-gate admission creates a spurious negative association among recruited porters.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (altitude acclimatisation) OR (load-carrying capacity)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(acclimatisation | ¬load_capacity, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(acclimatisation | load_capacity, selected) and show it equals P(acclimatisation). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between altitude acclimatisation and load-carrying capacity.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks load-carrying capacity must possess altitude acclimatisation to be admitted — hence P(acclimatisation|¬load_capacity,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has load-carrying capacity is admitted regardless of altitude acclimatisation, so P(acclimatisation|load_capacity,sel)=P(acclimatisation)=0.33. The gap (1.0 vs 0.33) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between altitude acclimatisation and load-carrying capacity observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.33+0.52-0.33×0.52=0.6784. (2) Among candidates without load-carrying capacity: only those with altitude acclimatisation are selected → P(acclimatisation|¬load_capacity,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with load-carrying capacity: selected regardless of altitude acclimatisation → P(acclimatisation|load_capacity,sel)=P(acclimatisation)=0.33. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬load_capacity raises P(acclimatisation) from 0.33 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.33,0.52
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6784)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.33)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
